svg.text: Three-node Raft HA: peer-add endpoint fires the seed without breaking existing users

g.text: create alice, verify on all three
create alice, verify on all three
a real addPeer payload is unreliable:
so the validation branch is used
3 ArcadeDB containers on one Docker network, all given the same Raft server list.
All containers start in parallel; Testcontainers waits for each node's HTTP health probe.
Every node's cluster endpoint is polled once a second until one of them claims leadership.
GET /api/v1/cluster -> body contains "isLeader":true (the run fails after 60s)
The starting state: a user that every node accepts, so any later damage to user state is visible.
startContainers() + waitForRaftLeader(60) + waitForAllNodesKnowLeader(60), then create user alice on the leader
The peer-add endpoint is probed with an empty peerId: this test checks the wiring, not a real membership change.
POST {"peerId":"", "address":""} -> assertThat(status).isEqualTo(400) ("Missing required fields: peerId, address")
The real assertion: the best-effort user seed fired by peer-add must not disturb the user state already in place.
assertThat(loginOk(0)).isTrue(); loginOk(1); loginOk(2) - asserted directly, no Awaitility
The full seed mechanism (SECURITY_USERS_ENTRY emitted by PostAddPeerHandler) is covered in-process elsewhere.
RaftUserSeedOnPeerAdd3NodesIT covers the seed itself; this IT covers the Docker-level endpoint wiring
